title: Generic degree of a normalized algebraic dualizing complex
statement: Let $(A,\mathfrak m)$ be a nonzero commutative Noetherian local ring and let $\omega\in D(A)$ be a normalized algebraic dualizing complex [def-per-algebraic-normalized-dualizing]. Let $\mathfrak p$ be a minimal prime of $A$, meaning a prime ideal containing no strictly smaller prime ideal. Assume $\dim(A/\mathfrak p)=e\geq0$ is finite, with dimension defined by chains of prime ideals [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. For any integer $i$, write $H^i(\omega)_{\mathfrak p}=A_{\mathfrak p}\otimes_A H^i(\omega)$ for module localization, where $A_{\mathfrak p}$ inverts all elements outside $\mathfrak p$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. Then $H^i(\omega)_{\mathfrak p}\ne0$ if and only if $i=-e$.

proof.text: Put $R=A_{\mathfrak p}$ and $\mathfrak r=\mathfrak pR$. By localization-Noetherianity, $R$ is Noetherian. Apply the minimal-prime localization radical lemma with $I=0$: $\sqrt{0R}=\mathfrak r$. In particular $\mathfrak r$ is finitely generated, and the finitely-generated-ideal radical-power lemma with $I=\mathfrak r$, $J=0$ gives $n\ge1$ with $\mathfrak r^n=0$. Since extension of ideals respects products (expand products of their generators), $\mathfrak p^nR=0$. Also $R\ne0$: the equation $1/1=0$ would give $s=0$ for some $s\notin\mathfrak p$, contrary to $0\in\mathfrak p$.

Set $B=A/\mathfrak p^n$ and $\overline{\mathfrak p}=\mathfrak p/\mathfrak p^n$. The ring $B$ is nonzero local, with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m/\mathfrak p^n$: an element outside this ideal lifts to a unit of $A$. It is Noetherian because each ideal is the image of its finitely generated inverse image in $A$. The quotient-localization isomorphism gives $B_{\overline{\mathfrak p}}\cong R/\mathfrak p^nR=R$. A prime ideal contains $\mathfrak p^n$ exactly when it contains $\mathfrak p$: for $x\in\mathfrak p$, $x^n\in\mathfrak p^n$, and primality gives $x\in\mathfrak q$. Taking inverse images under quotient maps therefore identifies, preserving strict inclusions, prime chains in $B$ and in $A/\mathfrak p$. Consequently $\dim B=e$, every prime of $B$ contains $\overline{\mathfrak p}$, and $B/\overline{\mathfrak p}\cong A/\mathfrak p$.

By the quotient lemma, $\omega_B=R\operatorname{Hom}_A(B,\omega)$ is a normalized algebraic dualizing complex over $B$. The defining bounded injective representative of $\omega$ shows that its cohomology is bounded, and its cohomology modules are finite. The Noetherian pseudo-coherence criterion therefore makes $\omega$ pseudo-coherent; it also makes $B[0]$ pseudo-coherent, since $B$ is cyclic over $A$. In particular $\omega\in D^+(A)$. Localization is flat, so the hypotheses of flat derived-Hom base change hold both for first argument $B[0]$ and for first argument $\omega$.

Write $W=\omega\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}R$. Exactness of tensoring with a flat module implies, by applying it to cycles, boundaries, and their quotient, $H^i(C\otimes_A R)=H^i(C)\otimes_A R$ for every complex $C$. The same observation shows that ordinary tensor with $R$ preserves quasi-isomorphisms (it preserves acyclicity of cones); applied to a K-flat resolution $P\to C$, the K-flat model of derived change of rings then shows that $C\otimes_AR$ computes $C\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}R$. In particular $B\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}R=R$ by Step 1. Flat derived-Hom base change now gives $\omega_B\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}R\cong R\operatorname{Hom}_R(R,W)\cong W$. For the last isomorphism, choose a K-injective representative $J$ of $W$; evaluation at $1$ identifies $\operatorname{Hom}_R^\bullet(R[0],J)$ with $J$, including the differentials. Thus $H^i(\omega_B)_{\overline{\mathfrak p}}\cong H^i(\omega)_{\mathfrak p}$: localization over $B$ is tensor with $B_{\overline{\mathfrak p}}=R$, and agrees with tensor over $A$ by the same fraction map.

Apply the Ext bounds to the finite $B$-module $M=B$, whose support is all of $\operatorname{Spec}B$ and has dimension $e$. Indeed $B_{\mathfrak q}\ne0$ for every prime $\mathfrak q$ by the same fraction argument as Step 1. Evaluation at $1$ on the Hom complex, as in Step 4, identifies $R\operatorname{Hom}_B(B,\omega_B)$ with $\omega_B$. Thus for $N_i=H^i(\omega_B)$ we have $N_i=0$ unless $-e\le i\le0$, and $\dim\operatorname{Supp}_B(N_i)\le-i$. Each $N_i$ is finite because $\omega_B$ is a dualizing complex.

If $(N_i)_{\overline{\mathfrak p}}\ne0$, the finite-module support criterion gives $\operatorname{Ann}_B(N_i)\subseteq\overline{\mathfrak p}$. Every prime of $B$ contains $\overline{\mathfrak p}$ by Step 2, so the same criterion gives $\operatorname{Supp}_B(N_i)=\operatorname{Spec}B$. Its dimension is $e$. The bounds in Step 5 give $e\le-i$ and $i\ge-e$, hence $i=-e$. By Step 4 this proves that $H^i(\omega)_{\mathfrak p}=0$ for every $i\ne-e$.

The defining homothety isomorphism $A[0]\cong R\operatorname{Hom}_A(\omega,\omega)$ remains an isomorphism after applying the derived change-of-rings functor $-\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}R$, and $A[0]\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}R=R[0]$ by Step 4. Apply flat derived-Hom base change with first argument $\omega$ (its pseudo-coherence and boundedness were checked in Step 3). It gives $R[0]\cong R\operatorname{Hom}_R(W,W)$. If $W=0$, the right side is zero, as the derived-Hom complex of zero objects is zero. But $H^0(R[0])=R\ne0$ by Step 1. Thus $W\ne0$. This expands precisely the nonzero part of the source's final appeal to localization of dualizing complexes, without requiring normalization to be preserved by localization.

By Step 4, $H^i(W)=H^i(\omega)_{\mathfrak p}$. Step 6 makes every cohomology module except possibly $H^{-e}(W)$ zero. If this last module were also zero, the map from any representative complex of $W$ to the zero complex would be a quasi-isomorphism, so $W$ would be zero in the derived category. This contradicts Step 7. Hence $H^{-e}(\omega)_{\mathfrak p}\ne0$. Combined with Step 6, this is the required equivalence for every integer $i$.
